examples.title: Example 1: Implementing Basic Video Playback Features
examples.description: This example covers the basic features of video playback, including how to manage the control bar, use preview images, handle autoplay, adjust the playback speed, and respond to keyboard shortcuts (since API version 15, enableShortcutKey can be used for enabling keyboard shortcut response). Additionally, it demonstrates playback controller operations including play, pause, stop, seek, and AVPlayer reset, and shows how to implement first frame display (since API version 18, posterOptions can be used for setting first frame display options). Since API version 21, posterOptions supports configuring transition animation effects for video preview image changes through the contentTransitionEffect parameter of PosterOptions, along with related state callbacks.

examples.title: Example 2: Enabling AI Image Analyzer
examples.description: This example shows how to use the enableAnalyzer attribute to enable AI image analyzer.

examples.title: Example 3: Playing a Dragged-in Video
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to enable the Video component to play a video that is dragged into it.

examples.title: Example 4: Setting the Video Fill Mode
examples.description: This example shows how to set the video fill mode using the objectFit attribute.

examples.title: Example 5: Handling Errors with onError
examples.description: This example uses an invalid video resource path to demonstrate how the Video component can obtain error codes through the onError event, available since API version 20.

examples.title: Example 6: Dynamically Setting Attributes and Methods of the Video Component Using attributeModifier
examples.description: The following example demonstrates how to use attributeModifier to dynamically set the attributes and methods of the Video component, including AI image analysis features and playback event methods.
